description: Canonical consensus test vectors for AXIOM protocol conformance. Any correct implementation of Core must produce the expected outputs for the given inputs. Vectors are deterministic from fixed seeds. Regenerate with: cargo run -p axiom-core-logic --example generate_vectors

vectors.description: CL1: valid send transaction accepted
vectors.notes: Standard send, alice→bob, 500_000 atoms

vectors.description: CL1: invalid signature rejected
vectors.notes: Corrupted Ed25519 signature

vectors.description: CL1: insufficient balance rejected
vectors.notes: Balance 100, tries 500_000

vectors.description: CL1: dust amount rejected
vectors.notes: 100 < MINIMUM_TX_ATOMS

vectors.description: CL1: zero amount rejected
vectors.notes: Amount 0

vectors.description: CL1: wrong wallet_seq rejected
vectors.notes: wallet_seq=999, expected 1

vectors.description: CL1: determinism pin — same input same output
vectors.notes: Determinism pin — same input must always produce same state_id. If this diverges from CL1_ACCEPT_001, a consensus-breaking change was introduced.

vectors.description: CL2: validator accepts incoming TX
vectors.notes: Gateway validation

vectors.description: CL3: validator re-validation accepts — produced_state_id + new_balance pinned
vectors.notes: Differential anchor for the zkVM checkpoint: both VMs must agree on result, produced_state_id, new_balance and new_wallet_seq.

vectors.description: CL3: invalid client signature rejected
vectors.notes: Corrupted Ed25519 signature — checkpoint check 9.

vectors.description: CL3: insufficient balance rejected
vectors.notes: Balance 100, tries 500_000 — checkpoint check 11.

vectors.description: CL3: dust amount rejected
vectors.notes: 100 < MINIMUM_TX_ATOMS — checkpoint check 2.

vectors.description: CL3: non-first TX without prev_receipts rejected
vectors.notes: wallet_seq=999 makes this a non-first TX, so prev_receipts become mandatory and their absence rejects before the wallet_seq check.

vectors.description: CL3: consumed_state_id != stored state rejected
vectors.notes: S-ABR hash mismatch — checkpoint check 5.

vectors.description: CL5: a redeem without a cheque_claim_proof is refused before anything else (ChequeClaimProofMissing)
vectors.notes: 3 genuinely-signed cheques from val0/val1/val2 to bob, no claim proof. CL5's claim gate fires first; the IPC codec carries no cheque_claim_proof, so no CL5 vector can get past it over the wire (KI#49 D2-B).

vectors.description: CL5: forged cheque signatures rejected
vectors.notes: All sigs replaced with 0xAB

vectors.description: CL5: under-k cheque bundle rejected
vectors.notes: Only 2 cheques, need 3

vectors.description: CL3: valid FACT chain (3 Dilithium witnesses) verified end-to-end
vectors.notes: Reaches verify_fact_chain_inner_with_burn_skip — the CL5 FACT vectors never do (they stop at the cheque_claim_proof gate).

vectors.description: CL3: FACT chain whose tip does not bind to consumed_state_id is rejected
vectors.notes: Continuity/freshness break — MUST be distinguishable from the valid chain.

vectors.description: CL3: FACT link with fewer witnesses than its required_k is rejected
vectors.notes: Quorum gate on the chain itself — distinct failure from a continuity break.

vectors.description: CL3: a valid FACT chain whose witness certificates are NOT presented is refused (E_FACT_WITNESS_UNCERTIFIED)
vectors.notes: YP §26.17.6.5 B2. Same bytes as CL3_FACT_VALID_001 minus `fact_certificates` — the verdict must flip on the certificate set alone.

vectors.description: CL3: FACT chain that does not start at the sender's derived opening state is refused (E_FACT_ORIGIN_INVALID)
vectors.notes: YP §26.17.6.5 B1. The witnesses' signatures no longer match the link (previous_state_id is in the commitment), but B1 is judged FIRST — the reason must be the origin, not the signature.

vectors.description: CL3: a certified FACT witness whose Dilithium signature does not verify is rejected (FactInvalidSignature)
vectors.notes: VALID with witness[0].signature[0] ^= 0xFF. An implementation that does not verify witness signatures accepts this.

vectors.description: CL3: a presented witness certificate that does not verify to the roots is rejected (FactCertificateInvalid)
vectors.notes: VALID with certificate[0]'s first root signature corrupted. An implementation that trusts a presented certificate without checking its issuers' signatures accepts this.

vectors.description: CL3: a FACT link that counts the same witness twice is rejected (FactDuplicateWitness)
vectors.notes: VALID with witness[2] replaced by a copy of witness[0] — every signature is genuine, the quorum is not. An implementation that counts signatures instead of distinct witnesses accepts this.

vectors.description: CL5: valid FACT chain with 3 Dilithium witnesses
vectors.notes: FACT chain verification exercised in CL5 with real Dilithium signatures

vectors.description: CL5: broken FACT chain state_id rejected
vectors.notes: FactLink new_state_id set to zeros — state chain discontinuity

vectors.description: CL5: scarred FACT link accepted (receiver consented)
vectors.notes: Scarred links permitted in CL5 — receiver consented via scar-passcode

vectors.description: CL11: valid election — 15 seats resolved, chain hash correct
vectors.notes: CL11: valid election — 15 seats resolved from 15 nominations, chain hash correct. IPC codec pending — from_file test skips CL11.

vectors.description: CL11: seat mismatch — resolved set differs from new_cert.seats
vectors.notes: CL11: seat mismatch — resolved set differs from new_cert.seats. IPC codec pending — from_file test skips CL11.

vectors.description: CL1: a prev_receipt whose state_hash does not anchor the declared state is rejected (InvalidStateId)
vectors.notes: Was ORACLE_VBC_TOO_OLD_001. An oracle TX (witness VBC 17_281 ticks old) — but the anchor check fires first, so this pins state anchoring, NOT the YPX-012 §2.5 VBC-age rule.
